Mr. Tiezheng Li, Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of FinVolution, commented, “In the third quarter, we prudently navigated a challenging industry landscape in China, marked by tightened institutional funding and a rapidly evolving risk environment. We prioritized asset quality and balance sheet strength over near-term earnings, proactively moderating origination, tightening underwriting and focusing on high-quality repeat borrowers in our Chinese Mainland segment.

“Our two-engine model under our ‘Local Excellence, Global Outlook+’ strategy kept us profitable, with our Overseas segment delivering ongoing, steady growth and contributing 37.1% of total revenue this quarter. Overseas operating profit more than doubled year over year, and we added 2.8 million new borrowers overseas, up 27.3% sequentially, demonstrating that our overseas expansion continues to drive our overall development.

“We worked closely with our funding partners to restore funding supply in China and saw a steady recovery on funding over the course of the third quarter. Looking ahead, we will remain focused on compliance and asset quality in China as industry adjustment continues, while further expanding our overseas platform. Supported by our diverse markets, technology advantages and a healthy, low-leverage balance sheet, we are well-positioned to manage near-term headwinds and build lasting value for our customers and shareholders,” concluded Mr. Li.

Mr. Jiayuan Xu, Chief Financial Officer of FinVolution, continued, “Net revenues for the third quarter totaled RMB2.6 billion, down 24.8% sequentially, and net profit was RMB205.6 million, down 51.8% sequentially. Chinese Mainland segment revenue declined to RMB1.5 billion as a result of a smaller loan book. In our Overseas segment, revenue grew 10.9% year over year to RMB948.9 million, and operating profit more than doubled year over year to RMB62.1 million as the platform continued to scale.

“Our balance sheet remains robust, with RMB8.4 billion in cash and short-term investments, and our leverage ratio stands at 1.5x, a historical low. While we expect the institutional funding tightening and the more challenging credit environment in China to continue to weigh on our results in the fourth quarter, our solid first-half performance provides a cushion, and our full-year revenue guidance of RMB11.5 billion to RMB12.9 billion remains unchanged. We will maintain that disciplined approach going forward and focus on generating sustainable returns for our shareholders,” concluded Mr. Xu.

In October 2026, the Company entered into and completed separate, privately negotiated transactions with holders of its 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2030 (the "2030 Notes"), resulting in the repurchase of an aggregate principal amount of US$90 million of the 2030 Notes. Following settlement of the repurchase, US$60 million aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Notes remained outstanding.

For the first nine months of 2026, the Company deployed approximately US$71.1 million to repurchase its own Class A ordinary shares in the form of ADSs. As of September 30, 2026, in combination with the Company’s historical and existing share repurchase programs, the Company had cumulatively repurchased its own Class A ordinary shares in the form of ADSs with a total aggregate value of approximately US$548.4 million since 2018.

The Company's financial performance in the third quarter was negatively affected by the tighter institutional funding and a more challenging credit environment in China. The Company expects these conditions to persist into the fourth quarter, with a similar impact on its business. Despite these industry headwinds, as its solid first-half performance provided a cushion, the Company reiterates its full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to be in the range of approximately RMB11.5 billion to RMB12.9 billion.

The above forecast is based on the current market conditions and reflects the Company’s current preliminary views and expectations on market and operational conditions and the regulatory and operating environment, as well as customers’ and institutional partners’ demands, all of which are subject to change.

FinVolution Group is a leading fintech platform with strong brand recognition across China and overseas markets, connecting borrowers of the young generation with financial institutions. Established in 2007, the Company is a pioneer in China's online consumer finance industry and has developed innovative technologies and accumulated in-depth experience in the core areas of credit risk assessment, fraud detection, big data and artificial intelligence. The Company's platform, empowered by proprietary cutting-edge technologies, features a highly automated loan transaction process, which enables a superior user experience. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had 261.3 million cumulative registered users across China and overseas markets.
For more information, please visit https://ir.finvgroup.com.

We use non-GAAP adjusted operating profit, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP net profit, non-GAAP net profit attributable to FinVolution Group, and non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per share and per ADS which are non-GAAP financial measures, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures help identify underlying trends in our business by excluding the impact of share-based compensation expenses and expected discretionary measures. We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making.

Non-GAAP adjusted operating profit, non-GAAP operating margin, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP net profit, non-GAAP net profit attributable to FinVolution Group, and non-GAAP basic and diluted net profit per share and per ADS are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. These non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tool, and when assessing our operating performance, cash flows or our liquidity, investors should not consider it in isolation, or as a substitute for net income, cash flows provided by operating activities or other consolidated statements of operation and cash flow data prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company encourages investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.
